constraints: Inspect the 22 published conformance inputs in the actual backend source archive; do not infer archive contents from manifest selection.
Hosted Python 3.13 build job; portable offline comparison of selected regular members. No extraction, member execution, native compilation, throughput SLA or untrusted archive service.
Local verification uses only small synthetic archives and focused tests; whole distribution builds remain hosted.
alternatives: Python tarfile inspection with PyPA build frontend.
Go archive/tar streaming inspection with a standards-compliant build frontend.
Java Apache Commons Compress tar/gzip inspection.
Rust-based uv build frontend or Hatch build orchestration.
rationale: KEEP Python for this extension to the packaging checks: the standard library directly exposes regular-member type, size, duplicate names and bytes without extraction. The finite inventory is shared with the existing manifest check, avoiding two independently maintained path lists.

Go provides sequential tar access, and Java Commons Compress supports tar and gzip. Both are credible archive readers, but neither eliminates the application-specific inventory and equality checks. No native deployment or throughput constraint favors a compiled inspector; this is a functional fit decision without performance ranking.

PyPA build invokes the declared backend and confines its purpose to producing distributions. uv and Hatch offer build orchestration, but changing the frontend alone does not provide the missing member-content assertions. Retain the declared backend and add the actual archive comparison.

Six focused archive methods exercise exact bytes, missing/wrong root, duplicate names, size, links and directories. A separate isolated CLI exercise accepts a synthetic archive of all 22 selected inputs and rejects an altered input without emitting successful evidence.
limits: The local RED run recorded six missing-module errors before implementation, not six demonstrated production assertion failures. No backend source distribution was built locally.
The hosted workflow change has been statically checked, not observed running. Successful hosted evidence requires a later exact-head run.

Only selected exact member names are checked. Unselected entries and aliases are not validated; no extraction safety, complete dependency closure, installed-product qualification or archive authentication claim.

The archive reader scans a trusted locally built archive; no total archive size, member count, decompression or hard memory bound is asserted. A ten-minute hosted job timeout bounds job duration operationally.
No runtime/peer module changes and no hardware, MLS, CNSA, five-nines or tactical qualification.
